correctness.rationale: Under immediate-child accessibility, induction on remaining height identifies greatest ordinary bisimulation exactly with equality of (color, set of child descriptors); different remaining heights are separated by a sufficiently long iterated diamond. Any nonempty set of at most q available child types is realizable independently, with repeats filling any unused slots. This proves the exact type and level-count formulas. The recurrence gives t_(k+1)≥a t_k; after t_k is large, the q-element subsets give log t_(k+1)≥q log t_k−q log(2q). Subtracting the fixed affine threshold yields log t_k≥c q^k, while counting all colorings gives log t_k≤C q^k. Splitting levels at q^k comparable to h with a sufficiently small constant bounds the lower-height terms by O(log h·q^(h/4)) and the upper-height tail by O(q^h/h). At q^k comparable to h with a sufficiently large constant there are at least q^(h−k) types, realized on disjoint height-k subtrees to attain Ω(q^h/h). Thus the lower bound concerns the maximum, not every coloring. The one-color and unary cases have exactly h+1 classes; t_k+1 in the binary sequence means addition of one, not the successor index. Independent greatest-relation pruning over all 32,768 binary height-three colorings found maximum nine classes. The frozen Python verifier and its recorded five small cases were inspected, not run; the asymptotic estimate is analytic.
residual_risks: No all-height equality in the finite level cap is claimed. The fixed-palette, fixed-arity statement does not extend as stated to graded modalities or accessibility closure.
